description:

description: The Master of Public Administration in Environmental Science and Policy (MPA-ESP) program at the Columbia University School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) and the Climate School is a 12-month MPA program that trains sophisticated public managers and policymakers, who apply innovative, interdisciplinary, and sustainable solutions to environmental issues. The program’s students are aspiring leaders who want to tackle the world’s most difficult sustainability challenges. The curriculum is a unique combination of environmental science and public policy, which are taught as an integrated whole, with a greater emphasis on science than other, more traditional MPA programs. In the summer, students begin with a specially designed curriculum of core courses in management, economics, and quantitative analysis. At the same time, they take a parallel set of courses in environmental science, which include earth science, chemistry, ecology and toxicology. In the fall and spring semesters, students complete the core requirements by studying a set of interdisciplinary case studies in the Workshop in Applied Earth Systems Policy Analysis. They also choose an area of specialization from the five following choices: Climate and Energy; Water; Food and Agriculture; Urban Systems and Sustainability; and ESG and Corporate Sustainability. Students complete their degrees with electives chosen from a wide variety of courses at SIPA, the Climate School and other graduate schools at Columbia University. MPA-ESP graduates work in the public, private and nonprofit sectors in the United States and worldwide. They hold positions in federal and state governments, international organizations, consulting firms, and nongovernmental organizations.

description:
The Master of Science in Landscape Design (MSLD) program at Columbia GSAPP is a three-semester post-professional degree for students with a professional degree in landscape architecture, or architecture. The MSLD program aims to address the urgent and complex challenges of our time through design research. These challenges include the climate crisis, its impacts on biodiversity, resources, and environmental justice, as well as the need for alternative models of urbanization to support an equitable public realm.

The MSLD curriculum provides a unique platform for advanced design research, drawing upon the School’s leadership in urbanism and design, and leveraging its New York City location. Students develop a research- and design-based thesis during the intensive twelve-month program. The thesis is initiated in the summer studio and seminar with a focus on fieldwork and research methodologies, continues through the fall semester with a focus on advanced design and prototyping, and is finalized in the spring semester with a focus on thesis documentation and a public exhibition. The thesis sequence is supplemented with required and elective courses in history/theory, technology, and media, as well as opportunities for interdisciplinary study with the School’s other programs and the University at large.

The MSLD program takes an experimental and collaborative approach to the field of landscape architecture. It encourages students to think critically, and to push the boundaries of the discipline. Recent student theses have investigated a range of topics, including landscape representation, material ecologies, climate mitigation and adaptation, environmental justice, as well as the design of equitable public space. The program is enriched by a vibrant culture of events, lectures, and exhibitions, providing a dynamic learning environment for the next generation of landscape architects.
Program name: Master of Science in Landscape Design

description: The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics is an interdisciplinary community of scientists who share the common goal of understanding the fundamental molecular mechanisms of life. We are an academic department within the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons at the Columbia University Irving Medical Center and a member of the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences at Columbia University. Our diverse research interests span a wide range of topics, including gene regulation, signal transduction, molecular genetics, developmental biology, neurobiology, and cancer biology. Our methods encompass a wide range of modern experimental techniques including biochemistry, biophysics, structural biology, cell biology, molecular biology, genetics, chemical biology, and computational biology. These research programs are facilitated by state-of-the-art research core facilities in biomolecular screening, cryo-electron microscopy, proteomics, mass spectrometry, and X-ray crystallography.

description: The PhD program in Biostatistics provides rigorous training in the theory and application of biostatistical methods for research in the health sciences. PhD students gain a sophisticated understanding of the theoretical basis of biostatistical methods, and obtain the skills necessary for the effective application of biostatistics in collaborative health sciences research, and for the development of new biostatistical methodology. Our graduates have an excellent placement record in academia, industry, and government. The program requires 60 credits, including coursework in biostatistical and statistical theory and methods, a set of elective courses chosen by the student in consultation with their faculty advisor, a doctoral qualifying exam, and the successful completion of a doctoral dissertation. A distinctive feature of the PhD in Biostatistics at Columbia is that students are matched to a Research Assistantship in their first year. This provides students with hands-on experience in collaborative research and an opportunity to develop their own research interests from their first day in the program. Students can also elect to take advantage of the many other research opportunities available within the Mailman School of Public Health, the Columbia University Irving Medical Center, and the greater New York City area.

description: Chemical physics is an interdisciplinary field at the interface of chemistry and physics. It is distinguished from physical chemistry by a greater emphasis on the physical and mathematical aspects of the subject. The PhD program in Chemical Physics at Columbia is jointly administered by the Department of Chemistry and the Department of Physics. It offers students the opportunity to pursue research in a variety of areas, including experimental studies of the electronic properties of nanostructured materials, novel spectroscopic methods, and theoretical studies of condensed-matter systems, quantum dynamics, and electronic structure. Students receive a strong interdisciplinary education that prepares them for careers in research or teaching in academic institutions, national laboratories, or industry. Upon satisfactory completion of the program, students receive a PhD in Chemical Physics. Students apply to the program through either the Department of Chemistry or the Department of Physics. Admitted students take a core curriculum that includes courses from both departments and must satisfy the requirements of the department through which they were admitted. Detailed descriptions of the requirements can be found at the departmental websites.

description: The Ph.D. program in Communications is an interdisciplinary program, housed at the Journalism School, that draws its faculty and curriculum from a number of departments and schools across the university, especially Sociology, Political Science, and History. Students in the program develop an individually tailored course of study that combines work in communications with another discipline. Students normally take two years of course work, including a small number of required courses, but primarily a set of courses selected to meet their own interests. In their second year, students write a substantial research paper. After the completion of course work, students take a set of qualifying examinations. On the basis of these exams and their course work, students are admitted to candidacy and proceed to write a dissertation. All students admitted to the program receive a five-year fellowship, including tuition and a stipend. description:
The Ph.D. program in Germanic Languages and Literatures provides students with a comprehensive knowledge of the major periods and genres of German literature and culture from the eighteenth century to the present, while encouraging them to develop in-depth expertise in one or more specialized areas of interest. These may include particular literary or historical periods (e.g., the eighteenth century; the Goethezeit; modernism), genres (e.g., the novel; poetry; drama), or a specific theoretical or interdisciplinary field of inquiry (e.g., literary theory; intellectual history; philosophy and literature; visual culture; film studies; translation studies; gender studies).

Students are encouraged to take courses in other departments and programs, such as the Institute for Comparative Literature and Society, the Department of History, the Department of Philosophy, the Institute for the Study of Sexuality and Gender, and the Film and Media Studies program in the School of the Arts. Those with an interest in medieval studies can take advantage of the rich course offerings both at Columbia and, through the Inter-University Doctoral Consortium, at the CUNY Graduate Center, Fordham, the New School, NYU, Princeton, Rutgers, and Stony Brook. Students may also obtain a graduate Certificate in Comparative Literature and Society or in Feminist Inquiry.

The graduate program admits only Ph.D. candidates. Students will be awarded the M.A. and M.Phil. degrees en route to the Ph.D. We typically accept two to four graduate students per year. description:
The doctoral program in Slavic Languages and Literatures provides students with an advanced knowledge of Slavic literatures and cultures in a comparative, interdisciplinary context. Students in the PhD program specialize in one of the Slavic literatures (Russian, Czech, Polish, South Slavic (Serbian/Croatian/Bosnian), or Ukrainian), and choose a secondary Slavic literature or a comparative field as their minor field of specialization. The program places a strong emphasis on literary theory and cultural studies. Students are encouraged to take courses in other disciplines, such as art history, comparative literature, film, history, and philosophy, as well as in Columbia's regional institutes.

The program has particular strengths in nineteenth- and twentieth-century Russian literature and culture (prose, poetry, drama, and literary theory); in Czech literature and culture of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, particularly of the avant-garde; and in Polish literature and culture of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, particularly Romanticism and modernism.

The PhD program offers two free-standing MA degrees: an MA in Slavic Cultures and an MA in Russian Translation. For more information, see the MA programs page. Applicants interested in the MA in Slavic Cultures or the MA in Russian Translation should apply directly to those programs.

description:
The Master of Science in Computational Design Practices (MSCDP) is a new 3-term STEM-designated master’s degree at Columbia GSAPP that focuses on the development of new computational design approaches by which to address pressing contemporary social, cultural, and environmental challenges. From the design of buildings to cities, the discipline of architecture is increasingly influenced by a complex and high-volume flow of data. The MSCDP program educates a new generation of computational designers who can not only use but also create new computational design tools by which to understand and act on this data. The program empowers students to develop novel design workflows that harness the immense potential of computation to create more just, inclusive, and sustainable futures.

Students in the program apply advanced computational design skills to a specific “practice area” of their choosing—these can range from ecological simulation and climate-change modeling to responsive technologies, artificial intelligence, and urban analytics. Through a combination of required courses, specialized seminars, and independent research, students are empowered to engage with computation not only from a technical but also a critical and conceptual perspective. The program offers a hands-on and project-based curriculum organized around a year-long research thesis that students develop together with faculty.

The MSCDP program is open to applicants from a range of backgrounds including architecture, data science, engineering, and media arts. We welcome students who wish to augment their existing design skills with cutting-edge computational knowledge, as well as students with a strong technical background who wish to apply their work to design and the built environment. No prior programming experience is required.

description: The doctoral program in the Department of Biological Sciences is an interdepartmental, integrated program that offers a broad-based, interdisciplinary training in modern biology. Students in the PhD program in Biological Sciences pursue research in one of three training tracks: (1) Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics; (2) Cellular, Molecular, and Biomedical Studies; or (3) Neurobiology and Behavior. The program features a core curriculum that provides a foundation for more focused studies in a wide range of topics, including structural biology and biophysics, biochemistry, cell and developmental biology, genetics and genomics, immunology, microbiology, molecular biology, neurobiology, and computational biology. A fundamental part of the training is the development of research and analytical skills that prepare students to become independent and original scientific investigators. Toward this end, students spend the major portion of their graduate careers on independent laboratory research, culminating in a written dissertation. Before beginning thesis research, students must also gain teaching experience by participating as a teaching assistant in at least two courses.

description:
The Genetics and Development graduate program offers interdisciplinary training leading to the PhD degree. The program is part of the Coordinated Doctoral Programs in Biomedical Sciences at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. For students, this provides a diversity of research opportunities and a variety of courses and seminars.

Research in genetics and development has undergone a major revolution in recent years. This revolution includes the sequencing of entire genomes; the ability to identify genes, determine their functions, and define their roles in developmental pathways; and the ability to manipulate the genomes of model organisms such as yeast, C. elegans, Drosophila, and mice. The department is a major participant in these advances through a broad range of programs that encompass the following areas: developmental genetics of vertebrates and invertebrates, human genetics, molecular genetics of the cell cycle and of recombination and transcription, immunogenetics, and neurogenetics.

description:
The Ph.D. Program in Education Leadership, which is part of the Department of Education Policy and Social Analysis, prepares students for careers as university faculty and researchers focused on the leadership and improvement of K-12 school systems. Graduates of our program are employed in major research universities in the U.S. and around the world, as well as in research and policy organizations.

Through a rigorous program of study that typically requires four to five years to complete, students in our program develop expertise in a core curriculum of education leadership, policy, and organizational theory as well as in quantitative and qualitative research methods. They take a wide range of elective courses and work closely with faculty advisors to design individualized courses of study and major research projects that build on and extend their particular interests. The program culminates in a doctoral dissertation that makes a significant and original contribution to the knowledge base on education leadership and school improvement.

At the core of the program is a faculty-student community with a shared interest in understanding and improving leadership in schools and school systems. Students and faculty in our program are addressing some of the most pressing questions in K-12 education: How can leaders create excellent and equitable schools for all students? How do education policies and politics shape the work of school leaders? And how can schools be organized and led to promote powerful teaching and learning?

description: The doctoral program in Mathematics Education is intended for persons who show promise of becoming leaders in the local, national, and international mathematics education community. The program prepares individuals for a variety of positions including university professorships, curriculum development, state or local supervision of mathematics, or research in mathematics education. The Ph.D. program requires a minimum of 75 graduate credits, of which at least 45 must be taken at Teachers College. The program of study for each student is planned on an individual basis. Each student is expected to develop a general knowledge of the different areas of mathematics education, to gain specialized knowledge in at least one area, and to obtain a broad understanding of related fields of inquiry. In particular, each student's program must include courses in mathematics education, mathematics, and other areas of education. All doctoral students are required to participate in a research apprenticeship for at least two semesters, working with a faculty member on one of his or her research projects. Also, all students are required to take an active part in the departmental seminars, a weekly colloquium where faculty, students, and visitors present their current work in an informal setting. A certification examination in two parts is required for the Ph.D. degree. The first part, on mathematics, is usually taken at the beginning of the second year of study. The second part, on mathematics education, is taken when the student has completed most of his or her coursework. Upon completion of the coursework and certification examinations, the student, with his or her advisor, forms a dissertation committee and prepares a dissertation proposal. The final requirement for the Ph.D. degree is the successful completion and defense of a dissertation. The dissertation must be a substantial piece of original research that makes a significant contribution to the field of mathematics education.

A unique and defining aspect of the doctoral program is its emphasis on mentoring doctoral students into the profession. Every doctoral student works with one or more faculty members as a research apprentice, and as a teaching apprentice. As a research apprentice, students learn to design and conduct research, to prepare manuscripts for publication, and to prepare research proposals for funding. description:
The Ph.D. program in English and Comparative Literature at Columbia has long been a distinguished one. It is a program that combines broad coverage of literary history with a timely engagement with theoretical and interdisciplinary concerns. While the department has traditional strengths in English and American literary history, students' interests are various, ranging over all the periods of English and American literary history and including literary theory, gender studies, post-colonialism, cultural studies, and African-American studies. In all these areas, the faculty has unusual distinction and depth. A number of the faculty are associated with the School of Criticism and Theory, and with the various centers and institutes on campus, such as the Institute for Research on Women, Gender, and Sexuality, the Institute for Research in African-American Studies, the Institute for Comparative Literature and Society, the Center for the Study of Ethnicity and Race, and the Heyman Center for the Humanities.

The program is extremely flexible; it has few specific requirements beyond a total of ten courses and a set of distribution requirements. Many of our students take courses in other departments and programs, and with the members of the Inter-University Doctoral Consortium (NYU, CUNY Graduate Center, Princeton, the New School, Stony Brook, Rutgers, and Fordham).

description: The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences (DEES) at Columbia University is an internationally recognized leader in the earth sciences. At DEES, we believe that the future of our planet depends on a deeper understanding of the earth. We use the tools of basic science to study the planet, from its core to its atmosphere, and to understand its past, present, and future. Through research, education, and outreach, we seek to advance our understanding of the earth and to share this knowledge for the benefit of all people. We are a diverse and welcoming community of scientists with a wide array of expertise and interests. Our department is part of the Columbia Climate School and is the home department for the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, one of the world's leading research centers devoted to the study of the earth. The department’s areas of strength include solid earth geophysics (seismology, geodynamics, marine geophysics, and rock mechanics), geochemistry (low-temperature, high-temperature, and isotope), oceanography (physical and chemical), paleoclimatology and paleoceanography, climate science, atmospheric science, geobiology, and environmental science. A special focus exists for the study of climate change, both past and future. The graduate program prepares students for careers in research and teaching. Many PhD students continue their studies as postdoctoral scholars and then go on to faculty or research positions at universities or research institutions such as Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. Others pursue careers in environmental consulting, the energy and mining industries, finance, and other fields.
Program name: PhD in Geology and Earth Science

description: The graduate program in the Department of Germanic Languages is designed to lead to the Ph.D. degree in German Literature and Cultural History. The department specializes in literary history and theory, intellectual history, and critical theory. Faculty research interests include Medieval studies; early modern literature and culture; the Enlightenment; Romanticism and nineteenth-century studies; Classicism and modernism; literary theory; critical theory and philosophy; film and media studies; Holocaust studies; and Yiddish studies. Students work closely with faculty members in small seminars and on individual research projects. We offer generous funding for up to six years, including five years of fellowship and one year of teaching. We are often able to support students beyond the sixth year as well. description: The Ph.D. program in the Department of Art History and Archaeology at Columbia University is a vigorous and intellectually challenging course of study that trains students in the histories and theories of art, architecture, and archaeology. description: The Ph.D. in Historic Preservation is a research-based degree focused on the history, theory, and practice of historic preservation and its relationship to the conservation and management of the built environment. As a discrete field of inquiry, historic preservation is a form of cultural and historical inquiry that engages a wide range of methods and theories. The Ph.D. program in Historic Preservation at GSAPP recognizes the multidisciplinary character of the field and requires students to engage critically and deeply with a broad range of historical and theoretical discourses. The program is designed to be completed in five years. Students take courses during their first two years, where they work closely with faculty to develop their own specialized fields of interest and prepare for their qualifying examinations. The final three years of the program are dedicated to the research and writing of a doctoral dissertation. While the Ph.D. program in Historic Preservation is separate from the M.S. program in Historic Preservation, students in both programs take some courses together. The doctoral program seeks to foster a community of scholars within the School and take advantage of the diverse curricular offerings and faculty at GSAPP as well as the larger University community.

description: The Department of Physics offers a graduate program leading to the Ph.D. degree in physics. The first two years of the graduate program are devoted to advanced courses in physics and to starting research. Students are expected to complete the written qualifying examination by the start of their second year, and take an oral examination in the spring of their second year. Most students will have chosen a thesis adviser and started a research project by the end of their second year. The following years are devoted to research, culminating in a thesis. The department has a broad research program, with active experimental and theoretical research in astrophysics and cosmology, atomic-molecular-optical physics, condensed matter physics, gravitational physics, high energy nuclear physics, and high energy particle physics. description: The Ph.D. Program in Clinical Psychology at Teachers College, Columbia University has a proud history and a long-standing reputation for excellence. We were one of the first programs to be accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA) in 1947, and we have been continuously accredited by the APA since that time. Our program is a "scientist-practitioner" program (also known as the "Boulder Model") in which we train our students to be both scientists and practitioners. We believe that clinical practice should be evidence-based and informed by the latest research, and that research should be clinically relevant and informed by the complexities of clinical practice. Our program offers excellent training in research and clinical work with a wide range of populations. Our graduates go on to work in a variety of settings, including academia, hospitals, community mental health centers, and private practice. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment in which all students can thrive. We believe that a diverse student body enriches the learning environment and prepares our students to work with a diverse range of clients. We are also committed to social justice and to using psychology to make a positive impact on the world.

description:
The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences (DEES) offers a PhD program for students interested in studying the Earth, from its core to its atmosphere, from the geologic past to the Anthropocene. Our Department is a core component of the new Columbia Climate School, which leverages the University's pathbreaking research in earth and climate sciences and a multi-disciplinary network of world-renowned scholars and practitioners. The Department also forms the core of the Earth and Environmental Sciences division of Columbia’s Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, our world-class research campus on the west bank of the Hudson River, just north of New York City.

Our faculty and research scientists study the solid Earth, oceans, atmosphere, climate, and biosphere, on time scales from days to billions of years. Faculty and students pursue fundamental research on the nature of the Earth and its climate system, but are also engaged in applying this knowledge to the practical problems of sustainability in the Anthropocene, including climate change, natural hazards, resource depletion, and environmental degradation.

As a student in DEES, you will join an active community of researchers at Lamont-Doherty, with access to state-of-the-art laboratories and other facilities on the Lamont and Morningside campuses. Our Department and its members are committed to the principles of inclusion, diversity, equity, and anti-racism. All students accepted into the PhD program receive full financial support, including a tuition waiver, stipend, and health insurance.

description: The PhD program in Latin American and Iberian Cultures at Columbia offers a comprehensive curriculum that combines broad historical coverage of the literatures and cultures of Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula with a comparative and interdisciplinary approach. LAIC students work on a wide variety of research topics, from medieval Spain and colonial Latin America to modern and contemporary Iberia, the Southern Cone, the Andes, Brazil, the Caribbean, and the US Latinx world. Students are admitted into a single PhD track, though they may choose to specialize in Latin American, Iberian, or Luso-Brazilian studies. description:
The Master of Science in Building Science and Technology (MS-BST) is an advanced research-based degree that educates students to become experts in building sciences and technology. The program offers a platform for developing fundamental knowledge and acquiring skills for research in building sciences and technologies. Students develop research methods for scientific inquiry, design experimental research, build prototypes, and learn to operate advanced equipment. They graduate with deep knowledge of building science, technology, and research methods.

The curriculum requires students to focus on a particular area of building science and develop a thesis. The study areas include building envelope, thermal performance, moisture transport, passive house design and construction, building materials, material science, advanced manufacturing and construction, building structures, structural design, structural optimization, robotics, building systems, mechanical systems, sustainable technologies, energy conservation, daylighting, lighting, water conservation, and building performance simulation and analysis. The thesis can be in the format of a research paper ready for submission to a peer-reviewed academic journal or a proof-of-concept for a technology, material, or product with commercialization potential.

Students have access to the building science and technology laboratories at GSAPP, which provides access to state-of-the-art equipment for environmental simulation, building performance analysis, and development of building systems and materials. Students work closely with the faculty on their thesis topics and research projects. With the knowledge and experience gained in the MS-BST program, graduates are qualified to develop a career in research, industry, or pursue a PhD degree.

description:
The Master of Science in Anatomy program is part of the Department of Anatomy and Cell Biology and is housed at the Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons. It can be completed in two years of part-time study or one year of full-time study.

This program introduces students to the core concepts of the anatomical sciences, including human gross anatomy, microscopic anatomy, developmental anatomy, and neuroanatomy. All courses include lecture and laboratory components, and the human gross anatomy course includes a full-body dissection.

In addition to our core curriculum, students will participate in a one-year journal club in which they learn how to read, present, and analyze primary anatomical literature. description:
The M.A. in Climate and Society is a 12-month interdisciplinary Master of Arts program that trains professionals and academics to understand and cope with the impacts of climate variability and climate change on society and the environment. The program is offered by the Columbia Climate School, in partnership with the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences.

Drawing on the unparalleled educational and research resources of Columbia University, the Climate and Society program provides a unique educational experience. Our students come from a wide variety of backgrounds, but they share a common goal: to tackle the climate crisis.

A defining feature of the program is its interdisciplinary scope. Our students gain a solid foundation in climate science and learn to apply that knowledge to real-world decision-making. The curriculum is designed to be completed in 12 months, and is composed of five core courses, five electives and a summer internship or research. Students are trained to critically assess and apply climate information at various timescales, from seasonal forecasts to multi-decadal projections of climate change. Electives are chosen from a wide range of courses offered across the University, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests. Popular areas of study include food systems, water management, environmental policy, and energy.

Our students are prepared for careers in government, business, non-profits and academic research. They benefit from a dedicated professional development team that organizes workshops, career fairs, and networking events, as well as an active and engaged alumni network.

description:
The Master of Arts in Linguistics, Interpretation, and Translation at Columbia’s School of Professional Studies offers a comprehensive and flexible curriculum that blends academic rigor with practical application, empowering students to excel as interlingual communication professionals in diverse global settings. The program is designed for students seeking advanced training in linguistics, interpretation, and translation, as well as for those looking to transition into these fields.
The M.A. in Linguistics, Interpretation, and Translation is meticulously structured around three core pillars: linguistics, interpretation, and translation. This tripartite approach ensures a deep and holistic understanding of language and communication, preparing students for the multifaceted challenges of the global linguistic landscape.
- Linguistics forms the theoretical backbone of the program, offering students a profound understanding of language structure, meaning, and use. This foundation is crucial for mastering the nuances of interpretation and translation.
- Interpretation studies focus on the practical skills of consecutive and simultaneous interpreting, equipping students with the cognitive and technical abilities to facilitate real-time, cross-lingual communication in various professional contexts, including legal, medical, and conference settings.
- Translation studies delve into the art and science of rendering written text from one language to another, emphasizing not just linguistic accuracy but also cultural and contextual appropriateness. The curriculum covers a wide range of genres, from literary and technical texts to commercial and legal documents.
Students can customize their learning journey by selecting one of the three areas of specialization: Linguistics, Interpretation, or Translation. This flexibility allows them to tailor their studies to their specific career goals and interests, whether they aspire to be linguists, professional interpreters, or translators. The program culminates in a capstone project or a master’s thesis, providing an opportunity for students to apply their knowledge and skills to a real-world problem or an in-depth research question.
Through a blend of theoretical coursework, hands-on practice, and a final capstone or thesis, graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers in the language industry, academia, government, and the private sector. They emerge as skilled linguists, interpreters, and translators, ready to bridge communication gaps and foster understanding in an increasingly interconnected world.
Program name: Master of Arts in Linguistics, Interpretation, and Translation

description: The two-year Master of Public Health (MPH) degree in Environmental Health Sciences provides students with a solid foundation in the field of environmental health, including toxicology, epidemiology, and risk assessment, as well as an introduction to basic public health disciplines such as biostatistics, epidemiology, and management and policy. With this foundation, students can begin to specialize in an area of environmental health that is of particular interest to them, pursuing more focused coursework in their second year. Upon completion of the MPH degree in Environmental Health Sciences, graduates are able to: Describe the genetic, physiologic and psychosocial factors that affect susceptibility to adverse health outcomes following exposure to environmental hazards. Describe the major chemical, physical, and biological agents that are the basis for human disease, and understand the transport and transformation of agents in the environment and the routes of human exposure. Understand the mechanisms of toxicity for the major classes of environmental chemicals and the major disease processes that result from these exposures, including cancer, developmental and reproductive toxicity, neurotoxicity, and immune system toxicity. Understand the basis of risk assessment, including hazard identification, dose response assessment, and risk characterization and be able to apply this knowledge to the development of risk management strategies and environmental policy. Understand the structure of regulatory agencies and the legal framework for environmental protection at the federal, state, and local level.
Accreditation status: The Mailman School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). CEPH is an independent agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education to accredit schools of public health and public health programs outside schools of public health.

description: The primary goal of the marketing doctoral program is to train students for a career in academic research. Students in the Marketing PhD Program choose one of two tracks: quantitative or behavioral. The quantitative track focuses on empirical and theoretical quantitative research for marketing problems. Students interested in this track typically have strong backgrounds in economics, statistics, and/or engineering. The behavioral track focuses on consumer behavior. Students in this track typically have backgrounds in psychology, sociology, anthropology, and other related fields. Regardless of track, all students are expected to take PhD courses in marketing, as well as in a number of other disciplines such as economics, statistics, and psychology.
